ghchronicle 2.6.2: what this release would change in the stores this configuration writes

influxdb  url=http://influx:8181 org=default bucket=github  (InfluxDB 3 Core 3.11.2)
  pending     1.0.0/gh_code_scanning_alert_item/state
              rows of gh_code_scanning_alert_item carry state and reason as tags: 40 rows, the oldest dated 2023-11-14
              why: a build before 1.0.0 tagged each code scanning alert with its state and the reason it closed, so an alert fixed after it was first read is two rows at one instant
              set aside: InfluxDB renames the table gh_code_scanning_alert_item-<time> and keeps it queryable for 24 hours before it purges it
              read again: security, since 2023-11-14, writing gh_code_scanning_alert_item only
              not coming back: the rows of 1 repository this configuration no longer covers: octocat/gone
              needs your word: reading it again does not bring back every row it holds (see not coming back), and those are gone once the set-aside is purged
  not needed  1.0.0/gh_dependabot_alert_item/state: no row of gh_dependabot_alert_item carries state
  note        2.6.0/gh_actions_cache_entry/sum
              the store holds gh_actions_cache_entry: 90 rows, the oldest dated 2023-11-14
              why: rows dated before 2.6.0 hold one entry of each cache and ref, not their sum; no API lists a past day's caches, so they are kept as they are
              nothing is changed
  pending     2.6.1/gh_discussion_comment/is_answer
              rows of gh_discussion_comment carry is_answer as a tag: 3 rows, the oldest dated 2023-11-14
              why: is_answer was a tag, so a comment read before and after its acceptance is two rows at one instant
              set aside: InfluxDB renames the table gh_discussion_comment-<time> and keeps it queryable for 24 hours before it purges it
              read again: discussions and outbound, since 2023-11-14, writing gh_discussion_comment only
              safe to apply unattended: GitHub serves the whole history, the old rows are set aside for 24 hours, and every row is this configuration's

loki
  nothing to migrate: a stream is its job, kind and configured labels, and a tag change moves none of them

telegraf  url=http://telegraf:8186/telegraf
  not needed  1.0.0/gh_code_scanning_alert_item/state: no release wrote this shape, and only a store that can be asked could show one a build before 1.0.0 left
  not needed  1.0.0/gh_dependabot_alert_item/state: no release wrote this shape, and only a store that can be asked could show one a build before 1.0.0 left
  note        2.6.0/gh_actions_cache_entry/sum
              written before the state file kept a record of which release first wrote it, so it may hold rows written before 2.6.0; this store cannot be asked
              why: rows dated before 2.6.0 hold one entry of each cache and ref, not their sum; no API lists a past day's caches, so they are kept as they are
              nothing is changed
  pending     2.6.1/gh_discussion_comment/is_answer
              written before the state file kept a record of which release first wrote it, so it may hold rows written before 2.6.1; this store cannot be asked
              why: is_answer was a tag, so a comment read before and after its acceptance is two rows at one instant
              drop gh_discussion_comment in the store behind Telegraf, then read discussions and outbound again through it with -backfill -families discussions,outbound
              needs your word: ghchronicle cannot reach the store behind Telegraf

graphite  addr=graphite:2003 prefix=github
  not needed  1.0.0/gh_code_scanning_alert_item/state: no release wrote this shape, and only a store that can be asked could show one a build before 1.0.0 left
  not needed  1.0.0/gh_dependabot_alert_item/state: no release wrote this shape, and only a store that can be asked could show one a build before 1.0.0 left

              why: rows dated before 2.6.0 hold one entry of each cache and ref, not their sum; no API lists a past day's caches, so they are kept as they are
              nothing is changed
  pending     2.6.1/gh_discussion_comment/is_answer
              written before the state file kept a record of which release first wrote it, so it may hold rows written before 2.6.1; this store cannot be asked
              why: is_answer was a tag, so a comment read before and after its acceptance is two rows at one instant
              on the Graphite host, remove the old paths, one node deeper than the new ones:
                find <storage>/whisper/github/discussion_comment -mindepth 11 -name '*.wsp' -delete
                find <storage>/whisper/github/discussion_comment -type d -empty -delete
              read again: discussions and outbound, with no bound, writing gh_discussion_comment only
              needs your word: only whoever runs the Graphite host can remove its files
